title: Desktop application, view model and widgets
objective: Prepare the desktop for a second photo surface when the library milestone starts: GPU slots keyed by a surface id.
context_summary: The desktop's shared mechanisms each have one path (one draft state machine and driver, the crop on it with a declared angle stepper, one start refusal, one frame presenter, an idle loop that is asleep, a descriptor-driven control path), its seams own their state, its layers are enforced by repository rules, evidence drives the shipped paths and the live-agent path, and each behaviour is tested once. What remains is roadmap groundwork, blocked until the library milestone starts. Decisions: docs/decisions.md "Post-consolidation review"; constraints: docs/design/post-consolidation.md; the desktop design: docs/design/develop-workspace.md.

tasks.description: Key the photo surface's GPU slots by a surface id carried in its primitive, so two surfaces can be on screen at once.
extra_context: Blocked: starts with the library milestone on the roadmap, whose virtualized browsing across many photos (a grid, filmstrip or side-by-side compare) is the first place a second photo surface would appear on screen at once.

Iced keeps one rendering pipeline per primitive type, and `luxforge-ui/src/photo_surface.rs`'s `PhotoPipeline` holds one set of slots for the whole application: four photo slots (`slots`), two viewport-region sets (`regions`) and the retirement accounting behind the overlap ceiling. Two photo surfaces drawn in the same frame today would overwrite each other's textures and uniforms, both would show whichever was prepared last, and both would re-upload every frame instead of only on a version change.

Key the pipeline's slots by a surface id carried in the primitive, and release a surface's slots by that id when it goes away. Library thumbnails do not need this: they can use Iced's own image widget with handles built outside `view()`, since the extra hop matters little for a grid of small images.

The owner's provisional overlap ceiling (one current and one retiring full-photo allocation of at most 512 MiB each plus two region sets of at most 32 MiB each, 1088 MiB in all) is one photo-texture budget shared by every photo surface (docs/decisions.md, "Plan refresh", 2026-09-28): a second surface draws from it, for example at display resolution, rather than doubling it, and the retirement accounting counts every surface's slots against it.

acceptance_criteria: Two photo surfaces can be shown in the same frame without overwriting each other's textures or uniforms, proved by a two-surface test.
A surface's GPU slots are released by its id when it is no longer shown.
Single-surface behaviour, including the version-gated upload, is unchanged.

steps: Add a two-surface test asserting each surface keeps its own textures and uniforms and that closing one releases its slots without disturbing the other.
Run the existing single-surface photo-surface tests to confirm no regression.
expected_results: The two-surface test passes; existing single-surface tests are unaffected.
